Let \(i_Z,i_A,i_X,i_Y\) be distinct vertices and suppose
\(D=\{i_Z,i_A,i_X,i_Y\}\), the edge set of \(G\) is exactly
\[
\{i_Z\mathbin{\to} i_A,\ i_A\mathbin{\to} i_X,
  \ i_A\mathbin{\to} i_Y,\ i_X\mathbin{\to} i_Y\},
\]
\(V=\{i_Z,i_X,i_Y\}\), \(W=\{i_A\}\), \(T=\{i_X\}\), and
\(Y=\{i_Y\}\).  Put
\(\mathcal Z=\mathcal A_{i_Z}\), \(\mathcal B=\mathcal A_{i_A}\),
\(\mathcal X=\mathcal A_{i_X}\), and \(\mathcal Y=\mathcal A_{i_Y}\).
Let \(p\) be a probability law on
\(\mathcal Z\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\).  Put
\(p_X(x)=\sum_{z,y}p(z,x,y)\), and assume \(p_X(x)>0\) for every
\(x\in\mathcal X\).  Write
\(p(z)=\sum_{x,y}p(z,x,y)\) and \(p(z,x)=\sum_y p(z,x,y)\).  Under
the displayed guards define
\[
 e_z(x)=\frac{p(z,x)}{p(z)}\quad\text{when }p(z)>0,
 \qquad
 m_{zx}(y)=\frac{p(z,x,y)}{p(z,x)}\quad\text{when }p(z,x)>0.
\]
For each \(z\) with \(p(z)>0\), define its observed profile by
\[
 \rho_z=\bigl(e_z,(m_{zx})_{x:e_z(x)>0}\bigr).
\]
Thus \(\rho_z=\rho_{z'}\) means that \(e_z=e_{z'}\) and that
\(m_{zx}=m_{z'x}\) for every \(x\) in their common positive support.  Let
\(\mathcal R(p)=\{\rho_z:p(z)>0\}\), and define
\[
 L_x(y)=\sum_{z:p(z,x)>0}p(z)m_{zx}(y),
 \qquad
 M_x=\sum_{z:p(z)>0,\ p(z,x)=0}p(z).
\]
Then the following conclusions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The law \(p\) is the observed marginal of a model in
\(\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T)\) if and only if
\(\lvert\mathcal R(p)\rvert\leq\lvert\mathcal B\rvert\).  Given an
injection \(\kappa:\mathcal R(p)\to\mathcal B\), an explicit realizing
model sends every positive-mass \(z\) to
\(f(z)=\kappa(\rho_z)\), uses the root row
\(\theta_{i_Z}(z)=p(z)\), uses
\(\theta_{i_X}(\cdot\mid\kappa(\rho_z))=e_z\), and on reached treatment
rows uses \(\theta_{i_Y}(\cdot\mid\kappa(\rho_z),x)=m_{zx}\).  Zero-root-mass,
unused-state, and unreached outcome rows may be filled by arbitrary
probability vectors.  If \(p\) is rational, all arbitrary rows can be
chosen rational, giving a rational realizing model on the original
alphabets.
\item On every feasible law, the sharp identified set of the full
single-treatment intervention vector is
\[
 \mathcal Q(p)
 :=\left\{\bigl(Q_M(x,\cdot)\bigr)_{x\in\mathcal X}:
 M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T),\ p_M=p\right\}
 =\prod_{x\in\mathcal X}\bigl(L_x+M_x\Delta(\mathcal Y)\bigr),
\]
where \(L_x=(L_x(y))_{y\in\mathcal Y}\).  Simultaneous attainment is
obtained in the model above by setting, for every assigned profile whose
\(X\)-row misses \(x\), the common outcome row
\[
 s_x=\frac{q_x-L_x}{M_x}\quad\text{when }M_x>0
\]
for a desired \(q_x\in L_x+M_x\Delta(\mathcal Y)\); when \(M_x=0\), the
row is irrelevant and may be arbitrary.  The choices are independent
across \(x\).  If both \(p\) and the desired vector \(q\) are rational,
this attaining model can be chosen rational.
\item The full vector is point identified if and only if either
\(\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert=1\), or \(M_x=0\) for every
\(x\in\mathcal X\).  Hence, when \(\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert\geq2\), point
identification holds exactly when \(p(z,x)>0\) for every \(z\) with
\(p(z)>0\) and every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
\item After exact comparison of the profiles, feasibility, all
\(L_x(y)\) and \(M_x\), and the point-collapse test require
\(O(\lvert\mathcal Z\rvert\lvert\mathcal X\rvert
\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert)\) guarded arithmetic operations.  The region has
the linear-size half-space representation
\[
 q_x(y)\geq L_x(y)\quad(x\in\mathcal X,\ y\in\mathcal Y),
 \qquad
 \sum_{y\in\mathcal Y}q_x(y)=1\quad(x\in\mathcal X).
\]
\end{enumerate}
statements.justification: The profile theorem gives an exact and computable fixed-alphabet completeness result for the entire categorical four-node hidden-functional family, with simultaneous sharp attainment.
statements.gap: Generic discrete partial-identification methods can characterize bounds numerically or by polynomial programs, whereas this result gives a closed guarded product-of-simplexes region and an exact finite feasibility criterion.
statements.consumer: A support-aware causal identification implementation can compare profiles, emit the linear region, and construct an exact original-alphabet witness without quantifier elimination.

statements.statement:
Let \(D=\{Z,A,X,Y\}\), let \(\mathcal A_Z,\mathcal A_A,\mathcal A_X,\mathcal A_Y\) be arbitrary fixed finite nonempty alphabets, and let \(G\) have precisely the edges \(Z\to A\), \(A\to X\), \(A\to Y\), and \(X\to Y\).  Set \(V=\{Z,X,Y\}\), \(H=\{A\}\), \(W=\{A\}\), \(T=\{Z,X\}\), and take the outcome set to be \(\{Y\}\).  For every \(M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T)\), every \(z\in\mathcal A_Z\), every \(x\in\mathcal A_X\), and every \(y\in\mathcal A_Y\), joint-treatment positivity entails \(p_M(z,x)>0\), and
\[
 P_M(Y=y\mid do(Z=z,X=x))
 =\frac{p_M(z,x,y)}{p_M(z,x)}
 =p_M(Y=y\mid Z=z,X=x).
\]
Thus the complete joint-intervention distribution is graphwide identified by a guarded conditional-probability circuit for arbitrary fixed finite alphabets.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(M=(G,\mathcal A,\theta)\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T)\).  Every sum below is finite because every alphabet in \(\mathcal A\) is finite.  Since \(W=\{A\}\), Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:qualitative\text{-}functionality}\) says that, for each \(z\in\mathcal A_Z\), the probability row \(\theta_A(\cdot\mid z)\) is a point mass on the nonempty finite set \(\mathcal A_A\).  Consequently there is a uniquely determined map \(f:\mathcal A_Z\to\mathcal A_A\) such that
\[
 \theta_A(a\mid z)=\mathbf 1\{a=f(z)\}
 \qquad
 (a\in\mathcal A_A,\ z\in\mathcal A_Z).
\]

The stipulated edge set gives
\[
 \operatorname{pa}_G(Z)=\varnothing,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{pa}_G(A)=\{Z\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{pa}_G(X)=\{A\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{pa}_G(Y)=\{A,X\}.
\]
Thus Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:causal\text{-}factorization}\) and the preceding point-mass representation imply, for every \((z,a,x,y)\in\mathcal A_Z\times\mathcal A_A\times\mathcal A_X\times\mathcal A_Y\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_M(z,a,x,y)
 &=\theta_Z(z)\theta_A(a\mid z)\theta_X(x\mid a)\theta_Y(y\mid a,x)\\
 &=\theta_Z(z)\mathbf 1\{a=f(z)\}\theta_X(x\mid a)\theta_Y(y\mid a,x).
\end{aligned}
\]
By the definition of the observed marginal, \(V=\{Z,X,Y\}\), and \(H=\{A\}\), summation over the hidden state gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 p_M(z,x,y)
 &=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_A}P_M(z,a,x,y)\\
 &=\theta_Z(z)\theta_X(x\mid f(z))\theta_Y(y\mid f(z),x).
\end{aligned}
\]
Summing this identity over \(y'\in\mathcal A_Y\), and using normalization of the conditional-probability row \(\theta_Y(\cdot\mid f(z),x)\), yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 p_M(z,x)
 &=\sum_{y'\in\mathcal A_Y}p_M(z,x,y')\\
 &=\theta_Z(z)\theta_X(x\mid f(z))
   \sum_{y'\in\mathcal A_Y}\theta_Y(y'\mid f(z),x)\\
 &=\theta_Z(z)\theta_X(x\mid f(z)).
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(T=\{Z,X\}\), Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:joint\text{-}treatment\text{-}positivity}\), applied to the joint treatment assignment \((z,x)\in\mathcal A_Z\times\mathcal A_X\), entails
\[
 p_M(z,x)=P_M(T=(z,x))>0.
\]
This is the strict support guard needed for the only division below.  Hence
\[
 \frac{p_M(z,x,y)}{p_M(z,x)}
 =\theta_Y(y\mid f(z),x)
 =p_M(Y=y\mid Z=z,X=x).
\]
The ratio is an observable-law functional; it has not been identified with the causal target by definition.

To establish that identification, apply Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:truncated\text{-}intervention}\).  Under \(do(Z=z,X=x)\), the rows at \(Z\) and \(X\) are replaced by point masses at \(z\) and \(x\), while the mechanisms at \(A\) and \(Y\) remain unchanged.  Marginalizing the remaining non-outcome vertex \(A\) therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_M(Y=y\mid do(Z=z,X=x))
 &=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_A}\theta_A(a\mid z)\theta_Y(y\mid a,x)\\
 &=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_A}\mathbf 1\{a=f(z)\}\theta_Y(y\mid a,x)\\
 &=\theta_Y(y\mid f(z),x).
\end{aligned}
\]
Combining the last two displays proves, for every \(z\in\mathcal A_Z\), \(x\in\mathcal A_X\), and \(y\in\mathcal A_Y\),
\[
 P_M(Y=y\mid do(Z=z,X=x))
 =\frac{p_M(z,x,y)}{p_M(z,x)}
 =p_M(Y=y\mid Z=z,X=x).
\]

Finally, let \(M,M'\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T)\) have the same observed law \(p\).  The equality just proved, applied once to each model, gives
\[
 P_M(Y=y\mid do(Z=z,X=x))
 =\frac{p(z,x,y)}{p(z,x)}
 =P_{M'}(Y=y\mid do(Z=z,X=x))
\]
for every \(z,x,y\), where \(p(z,x)>0\) follows from joint-treatment positivity in either model.  Thus the complete joint-intervention distribution is constant on every observed-law fiber.  The map \(p\mapsto(p(z,x,y)/p(z,x))_{z,x,y}\) is therefore a graphwide identifying arithmetic circuit, and every one of its divisions is licensed by the mechanically entailed guard \(p(z,x)>0\).
statements.justification: The arbitrary-categorical theorem isolates the exact functional-node reduction: joint intervention fixes the parent of the hidden deterministic node and converts the causal target into a guarded observed conditional distribution without changing any alphabet.
statements.gap: Chen--Darwiche identification on their larger separate-marginal-positive class transfers to this joint-positive subclass, so the gain asserted here is an explicit fixed-alphabet reduction missed by ordinary ID on the latent projection, not a positivity-domain extension of their theorem.
statements.consumer: A constrained dosearch front end can recognize this family in time linear in its observed table and return the conditional-probability circuit with the joint-positivity guard attached.

statements.statement:
Let \(i_Z,i_A,i_X,i_Y\) be distinct vertices, put
\(\iota=(i_Z,i_A,i_X,i_Y)\), and suppose that
\(D=\{i_Z,i_A,i_X,i_Y\}\), that the edge set of \(G\) is exactly
\[
 \{i_Z\mathbin{\to}i_A,\ i_A\mathbin{\to}i_X,
   \ i_A\mathbin{\to}i_Y,\ i_X\mathbin{\to}i_Y\},
\]
that \(V=\{i_Z,i_X,i_Y\}\), \(W=\{i_A\}\),
\(T=\{i_Z,i_X\}\), and \(Y=\{i_Y\}\).  Write
\(\mathcal Z=\mathcal A_{i_Z}\), \(\mathcal B=\mathcal A_{i_A}\),
\(\mathcal X=\mathcal A_{i_X}\), \(\mathcal Y=\mathcal A_{i_Y}\),
and \(B=\lvert\mathcal B\rvert\).  Let \(p\) be a law on
\(\mathcal Z\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\) satisfying the separate
coordinate positivity conditions
\[
 p(z)>0\quad(z\in\mathcal Z),
 \qquad p_X(x)>0\quad(x\in\mathcal X).
\]
Use the guarded profiles, the profile-refinement partitions
\(\Pi_B(p)\), the response-kernel region \(\mathcal K(p)\), and the
saturation threshold \(B_{\mathrm{sat}}(p)\) from Definitions
\(\mathrm{def:profile\text{-}refinement\text{-}kernel\text{-}region}\)
and \(\mathrm{def:saturation\text{-}alphabet\text{-}threshold}\).  For a
model \(M\), define the causal response kernel
\[
 K_M(z,x,y)=P_M(i_Y=y\mid do(i_Z=z,i_X=x)).
\]
Then the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The law \(p\) is induced by a model in
\(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sep}}(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T,Y;\iota)\) if and only if
\(R:=\lvert\mathcal R(p)\rvert\leq B\).  On a feasible observed-law
fiber, the partitions of \(\mathcal Z\) into the nonempty fibers of the
functional map \(f:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal B\) are exactly
\(\Pi_B(p)\): the map may split an observed-profile class but may never
merge two distinct observed-profile classes.
\item On every feasible law, the sharp, simultaneously attainable set of
the full response kernel is
\[
 \left\{K_M:M\in
 \mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sep}}(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T,Y;\iota),\ p_M=p\right\}
 =\mathcal K(p)
 =\bigcup_{\pi\in\Pi_B(p)}\mathcal K_\pi(p).
\]
Every point is attained without changing any alphabet.  If \(p\) and the
selected kernel are rational, an attaining model can be chosen with
rational conditional tables.
\item Suppose \(R\leq B\).  At \(B=R\), the only admissible partition is
the partition into observed-profile classes, so for each profile \(\rho\)
and each \(x\in H_\rho\) there is one common free row shared by all
\(z\) having profile \(\rho\).  If \(\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert\geq2\), then
\[
 B_{\mathrm{sat}}(p)
 =R+\sum_{\rho:H_\rho\ne\varnothing}
 \bigl(\lvert\{z:\rho_z=\rho\}\rvert-1\bigr)
\]
is the least hidden-alphabet cardinality for which every missing
\((z,x)\) response row can vary independently.  More precisely, for
\[
 \mathcal K_{\mathrm{ind}}(p)
 =\left\{k:
 \begin{array}{ll}
 k(z,x,\cdot)=m_{zx},&e_z(x)>0,\\
 k(z,x,\cdot)\in\Delta(\mathcal Y)\text{ independently},&e_z(x)=0,
 \end{array}\right\},
\]
the region with hidden cardinality \(b\) equals
\(\mathcal K_{\mathrm{ind}}(p)\) for every
\(b\geq B_{\mathrm{sat}}(p)\), and is a strict subset for
\(R\leq b<B_{\mathrm{sat}}(p)\).  Intermediate cardinalities give exactly
the displayed finite union of profile-refinement polytopes.
\item On a feasible law, the full response kernel is point identified if
and only if either \(\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert=1\), or
\(p(z,x)>0\) for every \((z,x)\in\mathcal Z\times\mathcal X\).
\item Let \(Q_M^X(x,\cdot)=P_M(i_Y\in\cdot\mid do(i_X=x))\).  Projection
of the response kernel gives
\[
 Q_M^X(x,\cdot)=\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}p(z)K_M(z,x,\cdot),
\]
and its sharp region is
\[
 \prod_{x\in\mathcal X}\bigl(L_x+M_x\Delta(\mathcal Y)\bigr),
 \quad
 L_x(y)=\sum_{z:p(z,x)>0}p(z)m_{zx}(y),
 \quad
 M_x=\sum_{z:p(z,x)=0}p(z).
\]
If, in addition, joint positivity \(p(z,x)>0\) holds for every
\((z,x)\), then \(\mathcal K(p)\) is the singleton guarded circuit
\[
 K_M(z,x,y)=m_{zx}(y)=\frac{p(z,x,y)}{p(z,x)}.
\]
\item The family \(\Pi_B(p)\) can be enumerated by at most
\(B^{\lvert\mathcal Z\rvert}\) labeled block assignments after exact
profile comparison.  Each \(\mathcal K_\pi(p)\) has
\(O(\lvert\mathcal Z\rvert\lvert\mathcal X\rvert
\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert)\) simplex inequalities and linear equalities,
and all conditional divisions are guarded by the tested strict
denominators \(p(z)>0\) or \(p(z,x)>0\).
\end{enumerate}
statements.justification: The theorem gives the exact fixed-alphabet response-kernel region on the same separate-coordinate-positivity domain used by the functional-dependency reduction, including simultaneous attainment and the hidden-cardinality elbow.
statements.gap: Existing functional-dependency reductions do not give this original-alphabet union of profile-refinement polytopes or the least hidden cardinality at which every missing response row becomes independent.
statements.consumer: A support-aware front end for \(\texttt{dosearch}\) can compare profiles, enumerate compatible refinements, return the exact kernel polytope union, and collapse it to the guarded conditional circuit under joint positivity.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from the observed categorical law \(p\); no intervention data are sampled.
sampling_model.units: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent observations in the fixed finite space \(\mathcal A_V\).
sampling_model.treatment: The identification model imposes joint positivity \(p(T=t)>0\) for every joint treatment assignment; it does not impose strict positivity on all observed cells.
sampling_model.overlap: Regular Wald inference is restricted to a fixed support face with every active denominator at least \(\epsilon>0\); the confidence-map result allows guard uncertainty.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nonparametric nuisance fitting is required for the finite-alphabet multinomial plug-in; the covariance uses the empirical multinomial law and the active circuit Jacobian.

estimand_functional: On the separate-coordinate-positive arbitrary-categorical four-node class with hidden \(A=f(Z)\), feasibility is equivalent to \(R=|\mathcal R(p)|\leq|\mathcal A_A|\), and the sharp full response-kernel region is \(\mathcal K(p)=\bigcup_{\pi\in\Pi_{|\mathcal A_A|}(p)}\mathcal K_\pi(p)\).  Each partition refines the observed-profile classes; reached rows equal \(m_{zx}=p(z,x,\cdot)/p(z,x)\), while a missing row is shared exactly within its partition block.  The least cardinality giving independent missing rows is \(B_{\mathrm{sat}}(p)=R+\sum_{\rho:H_\rho\ne\varnothing}(|\{z:\rho_z=\rho\}|-1)\).  Projection by \(Q_M^X(x,\cdot)=\sum_zp(z)K_M(z,x,\cdot)\) gives the single-\(X\) region \(\prod_x(L_x+M_x\Delta(\mathcal A_Y))\); joint positivity collapses the kernel to the guarded conditional \(p(z,x,y)/p(z,x)\).  The binary rectangle is the binary-outcome corollary.  On every other certified success branch, \(q\) is the unique intervention vector returned by the active guarded leaf \(C(p,q)\), with every division licensed by an entailed strict-support guard.  An exact separating output proves that no graphwide functional of \(p\) equals \(q_M\); the residual formula \(\Psi_{\mathcal U}(p)\) remains only a doubled-fiber characterization and makes no identification verdict.
target_estimand: The causal target is \(q_M=(P_M(Y=y\mid do(T=t)))_{t\in\mathcal A_T,\ y\in\mathcal A_Y}\).  In the separate-positive categorical four-node specialization with \(T=\{i_Z,i_X\}\), this is the response kernel \(K_M(z,x,y)=P_M(i_Y=y\mid do(i_Z=z,i_X=x))\).  The observed conditionals \(m_{zx}\) are defined separately; the response-kernel theorem proves when they equal the causal target.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 18 uses separate marginal positivity for each treatment coordinate in its functional-dependency reduction; the converse construction in Appendix C may replace a parent state space by a Cartesian-product state space.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The response-kernel theorem works on that same separate-coordinate-positivity domain for the arbitrary-categorical four-node family and gives an exact original-alphabet sharp region, cardinality elbow, and simultaneous attainment.  It does not attribute fixed-alphabet preservation to Appendix C and does not claim a graph-general converse from that theorem.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5.1 and Algorithms 1--2 extract sufficient positivity for a returned formula, while Theorem 6.1 guarantees soundness when \(\mathsf{IDENTIFY}^{+}\) returns and supplies no converse from failed orders.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The response-kernel theorem derives every denominator guard directly and is complete only for the stated four-node family.  The graph-general guarded-ratio lane remains a one-way sound embedding; no failed \(\mathsf{IDENTIFY}^{+}\) order is treated as a nonidentification certificate.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 4 and Section 5 characterize identification by invariant cuts, but complete constrained cut discovery beyond strict positivity is not supplied.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The profile-refinement response-kernel union is an exact family-specific invariant calculation; the general finite coefficient-identity lane and residual positive-support formula do not claim a complete graph-general recognizer.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Classical \(\mathsf{ID}\) returns an identifying expression exactly when no hedge obstructs the interventional query in the saturated semi-Markovian model.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The categorical functional family can be sharper than ordinary ID on its latent projection, while the general result retains only a one-way embedding of every classical-ID success; no fixed-alphabet hedge converse is asserted.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2.4 gives the finite canonical-SCM representation used to reduce sharp counterfactual bounds to polynomial optimization.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: On the categorical four-node functional family, the response-kernel optimization collapses to an explicit finite union of profile-refinement polytopes, and its single-\(X\) projection collapses further to a product of translated simplexes, both with original-alphabet attainment.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Discrete causal bounding problems admit sharp polynomial programs and epsilon-certified spatial branch-and-bound.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The categorical family theorem gives a symbolic exact sharp response-kernel union and closed-form projection rather than a numerical certificate; outside that family the residual semialgebraic encoding makes no identification verdict.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Root-control context-specific identification reduces to finitely many ordinary graphical identification problems.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The response-kernel theorem handles an endogenous non-root functional node by observable profile classes, their hidden-state refinements, and unreachable mechanism rows; the graph-general positive-support guarded-district problem remains open.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: General context-specific nonidentifiability is NP-hard, and the proposed state calculus is sound rather than a complete endogenous-functional recognizer.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The partition union is a complete finite calculation for the categorical four-node family, whereas the four-output graph-general front end retains a no-verdict residual and does not claim that state search decides every positive-support stratum.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: DML-ID compiles a fixed identified functional into an orthogonal estimator with asymptotic normality under nuisance-rate conditions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The branch-respecting inference results apply after the categorical theorem or another certified front-end leaf supplies a guarded finite-alphabet functional; no inference claim is made on a non-singleton response-kernel region or residual output.

tldr: Functional restrictions can identify effects that classical graphical algorithms miss, but they also create structural zeros and algebraic fibers that defeat an exclusively rational output language. The project seeks a complete fixed-alphabet procedure that first certifies consistency, then either returns a branchwise exact algebraic identifying certificate with mechanically justified support guards or returns two exactly encoded real-algebraic models with the same observed law and different full intervention distributions. The construction embeds every sound classical ID success without claiming the false fixed-cardinality converse, is stress-tested on a fully specified binary non-root functional-node instance, and supports multinomial inference that respects uncertainty about the active support branch while reducing to ordinary Wald inference on stable faces.

project_justification.gap: Chen--Darwiche Theorem 18 gives a reduction on the broader separate-marginal-positivity domain, but its converse construction may enlarge alphabets and does not impose a total exact output contract; Hwang et al. extract sufficient positivity for returned formulas but prove only soundness of that return guarantee; classical ID, invariant-cut search, and CSI algorithms do not deliver a fixed-alphabet joint-positive success-or-countermodel dichotomy.
project_justification.niche: Finite alphabets make functional maps and row supports enumerable, while nonnegative network polynomials make support consequences combinatorial; this creates room for a causal-structural algorithm stronger than post-hoc guard extraction but more informative than generic real quantifier elimination.
project_justification.fill: The proposed \(\mathsf{F\text{-}ID}^{+}\) architecture combines exact feasibility, reachable-support and algebraic stratification, guarded district recursion, and alphabet-preserving algebraic countermodel compilation, with rational certificates as a preferred special case, a sharp binary boundary theorem, and branch-respecting multinomial inference.

related_work: Chen and Darwiche (2024, Theorem 18 and its proof in Appendix C) supply the closest identification architecture: close observed-parent functional nodes, eliminate them, and transport same-law models. Positivity of every joint treatment assignment implies their separate marginal treatment positivity, so the present domain is narrower rather than an extension; fixed-alphabet preservation and a total success-or-exact-countermodel certificate are orthogonal output refinements, and the comparison is non-comparable overall because their last transport step may form a Cartesian-product parent state. Hwang et al. (2024, Theorem 5.1, Algorithms 1--2, and Theorem 6.1) provide the denominator-licensing calculus adapted here; on the common finite fixed-alphabet input scope, the proposed total dichotomy strictly strengthens only their soundness-when-returned guarantee by making every failure produce an exact pair. Shpitser and Pearl (2006) provide the classical ID algorithm and hedge completeness for saturated semi-Markovian models; the present fixed-alphabet class inherits every returned ID functional but need not inherit the converse. Chen and Darwiche (2025, Proposition 4 and Section 5) characterize identification through invariant cuts and state that complete cut discovery beyond strict positivity is outside their result, so that work informs rather than supplies the proposed recognizer. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (2019, Theorem 1) show the computational hardness of general CSI and give a sound state calculus; Mokhtarian et al.
